title: Immunometabolic and clinical determinants of the immune response following seasonal influenza vaccination in kidney transplant patients
summary:
Following a kidney transplant, patients must take medication that suppresses the immune system to prevent the body from rejecting the new kidney. However, this increases the risk of infections, such as those caused by influenza viruses. At the same time, the immune response to a flu jab may be weakened.
In this study, we are investigating how the immune system of kidney transplant patients responds to the flu vaccine and which factors influence this response. To this end, blood samples are analysed at various time points and the results are compared with previously published reference values from healthy individuals.
The aim is to gain a better understanding of the immune response following a flu vaccination in kidney transplant recipients and, in the long term, to contribute to the improvement of vaccination strategies.
conditions: Need for immunization against certain single viral diseases

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Age ≥ 18 years.
• Capacity to give consent and willingness to participate voluntarily in the study.
• No known infection with hepatitis B, hepatitis C or HIV.
• Previous kidney transplant, regardless of the time since the transplant (< 6 months or ≥ 6 months).
Exclusion criteria:
• Underage (under 18 years of age)
• Lack of capacity to give consent or inability to provide
informed consent in writing
• Existing viral infections, in particular hepatitis B, hepatitis C or HIV.
• Pregnancy or breastfeeding
